chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would have a two-year-old camel as a debt, so he would give back the four-year-old one.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on repaying a debt with a better quality item?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the Prophetic practice of 'Ihsan' (excellence) in financial transactions, where the debtor provides the superior quality ('Arba') when the specific type is not strictly defined, going beyond mere contractual obligation. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a foundational evidence for the virtue of settling debts with generosity, distinguishing between the minimum legal requirement ('Adl') and the recommended ethical standard. It underscores the spiritual merit of clearing one's dues with the best available assets, reflecting the Prophet's (SAWW) character in commercial dealings.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, when there happened to be the (debt of) a five-year old camel upon him<sup>saww</sup>, gave back the heavier one’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from abu Maryam who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause,
whenever owing something to someone would pay back heavier.’”
